# The L3 application dispatch's release — step 5, the release check: findings (2026-11-16)

**What this file is.** The findings of step 5 of handoff entry 767 §3, the release check, by sittings that edited none
of the dispatch (`records/cc/instructions/cc_instruction_l3_application_2026_11_08.md`). It decides nothing and edits
nothing. Working practice only; no algorithm change; no documentation of the specification changed.

**The split, on the user's word "agreed" (2026-11-16, the sitting booted on entry 1024).** Step 5 is done in five parts,
in this order: (1) the row check, in slices of consecutive rows of the working file
(`ratification_surfaces/cowork_l3_application_release_edit_order_2026_11_14.md`), **findings only, no dispatch edit**;
(2) the carried items (the premise ledger at its objects; the dispatch's line 60 items (1) to (7) at their objects;
whether anything of Part B is still open; entry 1024 §2 item 2; what entries 1015 to 1023 §2 list for step 5);
(3) the D-250 revalidation against the tree as it then stands; (4) the corrections, every finding of parts 1 to 3
applied at its site, former wordings kept, the wordings shown to the user before landing; (5) a check by a session that
made none of the corrections: the corrections themselves, the D-434 self-check recorded, and the sweep for absolutes
and paraphrase. Ground: the user's aim of 2026-11-12 (the dispatch must not reach Claude Code incomplete, incorrect or
incoherent) and entry 767 §3's rule that the dispatch is checked by a session that did not edit it. This departs from
entry 767 §3 step 5's words *"Corrections at their sites"*, which would have each slice edit as it goes; the user agreed
to the departure.

**How a row is checked.** The row is read in the working file; the dispatch is read at the place the row names,
located by the row's quoted text (a row's *"Now at dispatch lines"* is as the dispatch stood when its batch landed;
later batches and release step 3 moved it). The check asks whether the dispatch now carries what the row says was
applied (or, for a row ordering no edit, that the quoted text stands), former wordings included. It does not re-derive
a row from its ruling record; that was the site table's work. Dispatch line numbers below are the dispatch at 874,206
bytes, 7,102 lines (2026-11-16).

## The user's ruling of 2026-11-18 on what the sweep checks (recorded by the sitting booted on entry 1105)

**The ruling, in the user's words.** Given in the sitting booted on entry 1104; recorded here on his order in the opening instruction of the sitting booted on entry 1105: *"check only claims that steer Claude Code's acts (counts, row lists, dispositions, pointers it must follow) and leave pure wording to after the release."* It changes entry 1105 §3 step 1, the sweep of §L from §L.24's heading (dispatch line 2477) to Task 0's heading (line 5868), from the sitting booted on entry 1105 onward; this sitting reads it as not reopening the sections above this one. Working practice only; no algorithm change; no documentation of the specification changed.

**How the remaining sittings apply it.** Checked at the objects: every count (check sums, a record's population, arithmetic); every row list and every row's disposition (the *Reading file — rows* tables, the rows a record mentions and does not place, transfer lists, rows named by more than one record); every pointer Claude Code must follow (paths, record lines, list items, rulings named as answering an *Open* point, the Tasks and forms named); the act's search, since it decides which form carries a row; and what an entry orders written or not written (its *Successor*, *Charter*, *Interface contract*, *L2 sides* and *Register* lines and its paragraphs on decisions-register identities). Left to after the release, not checked: whether a quotation that only describes a record is faithful (each entry's opening paragraph, *Alternatives offered and not taken*, *Carried open by the record*); the dated notes (★ notes, *Written …*) and the former wordings kept, which record earlier sittings; and the sweep's words where they claim something about wording only. A wording defect seen in passing is noted in one line as left to after the release, and not pursued. **A reading, open to the user's overrule:** words an entry orders Claude Code to write into a document (for example §L.24 amendment 1's *"The statements, as ratified"*) are taken as steering its acts, because a wrong quotation there is what Claude Code would write.

**The remainder, sized again under the ruling** [estimated by a read-only script over the staged dispatch: each paragraph classed by its label, and the ★ notes and kept former wordings inside the kept paragraphs left out; an estimate, since a few ★ notes also carry answers given at release]. Of the 32 entries' 771 hits in 400,573 characters, about 504 hits in about 258,301 characters lie in the parts the ruling keeps, about two thirds; per entry, from about 3,500 characters (§L.45) to about 15,500 (§L.39). The larger saving is in the objects: a record or surface is no longer read whole to check every quotation, only at the places that hold the counts, rows, dispositions and pointers, found by search first. A row list that rests on a surface still needs that surface: §L.24's 50 relocated row-parts rest on the second and third cut surfaces' §2 and on the list's item (xlvii) [relayed from dispatch line 2505; not yet read at those objects].

**What changes for the remaining sittings.** A batch may hold more than one entry; each batch is still sized out loud before starting and stopped at an entry boundary, and a further batch is judged out loud after each. The section form (one row per entry, the rows and findings numbered on from row 191 and finding 82) is unchanged. The like items of §L.6, §L.11 and §L.13 to §L.15 are judged by the same test. At the rate of the last two batches (§L.22 and §L.23, one entry a sitting), the 32 entries would have needed 32 sittings; under the ruling the estimate is about half that or fewer, on the order of 12 to 16. That is a judgment, not a count; the first batch under the ruling will show the rate, and is reported against this estimate.

*Provenance: Cowork, 2026-11-18 (Stockholm), the sitting booted on entry 1105. The user's words: the opening instruction, which carries the ruling and the order to record it.*
